method: I describe the executed method as known Huber iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS), with no novelty claim. Let A=[1,X] include an intercept. Initialize beta_0=argmin_beta ||y-A beta||_2^2 using numpy.linalg.lstsq(rcond=None). The selected snapshots/initial_full/config.json specifies method=huber_irls, iterations=20, delta=1.345, scale=residual_mad, and scale_floor=1e-8. For t=0,...,19, compute r_t=y-A beta_t; s_t=max(median_i |r_t,i-median_j(r_t,j)|/0.6744897501960817,1e-8); c_t=1.345 s_t; and w_t,i=1 when |r_t,i|<=c_t, otherwise c_t/|r_t,i|. Update beta_(t+1)=argmin_beta sum_i w_t,i(y_i-A_i beta)^2 using square-root-weighted least squares. Predictions are [1,X_new] beta_20. These weights correspond to Huber loss rho(u)=u^2/2 for |u|<=1.345 and 1.345|u|-1.345^2/2 otherwise; residual scale is re-estimated each iteration, so execution is the stated iterative procedure rather than optimization with a fixed scale. Recorded selected mean validation MSE is 0.04132739672516235 on full validation and 0.048565701283490234 on subset validation, versus baseline values 1.99069057153675 and 6.408876466897288, respectively.
limitations: I read AGENTS.md, model.py, the selected configuration, and all 12 *_metrics.json files without editing files. Metrics are recorded results, not independently reproduced measurements. Every metric file identifies validation seeds 0-4 and extra=false; none supplies held-out-test or extra-seed evidence, timing, or memory measurements. Selection on these validation results does not establish generalization. seed0 has lower subset MSE (0.04281212939891291) but slightly higher full MSE (0.04135963917671087) than the selected method; evolved0 is worse on both (0.04961906615617495 subset; 0.04145129104587781 full). Ablation full MSEs are 1.99069057153675, 0.07206682832034102, and 0.04132739672516235; metric files alone do not identify the removed components or establish universal redundancy. The implementation assumes a linear relationship with an intercept and a one-dimensional target for active IRLS; it has no explicit regularization, leverage-point protection, convergence stopping rule, or explicit nonfinite-input validation. Twenty iterations do not certify convergence. Robust residual weighting does not guarantee robustness to arbitrary contamination. Known Huber IRLS on synthetic data is not scientific novelty.
